newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Eight Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Eight Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.

text.p: Eight East Timorese entered the French embassy in Jakarta early on Tuesday, diplomatic sources said.

The sources said it was not yet clear whether they were seeking political asylum, although the French embassy has been a regular gateway for more than a year for East Timorese who want to leave Indonesia.
"It is not yet clear where they want to go," one source said.
Since September 1995, 100 East Timorese who have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta have gone to asylum in Portugal, the former colonial power in East Timor.
A spokeswoman for the French embassy said she was not yet able to give out any information on the subject.
The Portuguese news agency Lusa said the eight entered the embassy in the early morning.
One diplomatic source said the group was thought to include university students from Bandung and Surabaya.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
The Indonesian government has allowed such asylum seekers to leave unhindered with their travel to Portugal facilitated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
